voice-assistant.faqTitle: What people ask about the phone assistant

faq.q: Do I have to change my number?
faq.a: No. The number stays yours and calls are forwarded to the agent. You can choose to send all of them, or only those nobody answers after a few rings, or only those outside working hours. Porting the number is not necessary.

faq.q: Can you hear that it is a machine?
faq.a: You can hear that it speaks cleanly and without pauses for thought. We do not hide it either: the agent says from the start that it is an agent. The point is not to fool anyone, it is that the person calling at 21:40 gets an answer instead of nothing.

faq.q: What does it do when it does not understand or does not know?
faq.a: It says so and takes the call further: it either transfers to a person, if somebody is available and the rule allows it, or writes the question down and asks for a contact number. It does not improvise an answer to end the call neatly — a price invented on the phone becomes a complaint the next day.

faq.q: How does it know what is urgent?
faq.a: From the rules you write. Urgent means something different at a clinic than at a car service, and we do not guess: together we set which words and which situations trigger a transfer, and to which number.

faq.q: How do I find out what was said?
faq.a: After every call you get a written summary: who called, what they wanted, what was agreed, what stayed open. What went into the calendar is in there too. The history stays in the portal, so you are not searching through emails a month later.

faq.q: What happens to call recordings?
faq.a: Recording is not switched on by default. If you switch it on, the caller is told at the start of the call, as the law requires, and you set how long recordings are kept. Each client's data stays separate.

faq.q: When will it be ready?
faq.a: We do not give a date we cannot keep. Its price is set, though, and if you reserve it now, at launch it stays what it is today.

configurator.faqTitle: What people ask about the configurator

faq.q: How is it different from an ordinary form?
faq.a: A form asks every question at once, and the same ones for everybody. The configurator asks the next question based on the last answer: if the person said installation is not needed, it does not go on to ask about floors and lifts. The fields stay the same, the road to them is shorter — which is why people reach the end.

faq.q: Does it give the customer a price?
faq.a: No. It collects the data the price depends on and hands the sheet to your salesperson. You do the pricing, with the margin and the exceptions you never write down anywhere. If you want an indicative price said in the conversation itself, that is the chatbot's job, from your own price list.

faq.q: What happens when the customer does not know the answer?
faq.a: It moves on and flags the point. The sheet arrives saying "to clarify: ceiling height", not with an invented value. An empty field you can see is cheaper than a full field that is wrong.

faq.q: Who writes the questions?
faq.a: We do, during setup, from the way you already work: what your salespeople ask, in what order, which combinations are impossible. They are changed from the portal, without asking us.

faq.q: When will it be ready?
faq.a: We do not give a date we cannot keep. Its price is set, though, and if you reserve it now, at launch it stays what it is today.

The price depends on the system, on the bone and on what has to be done first. The agent gives your range and explains why it cannot be a single figure, instead of staying silent until the consultation.
The recovery period decides when the person books time off. The agent gives it as a range, from the clinic's own protocol, and adds that the doctor confirms it at the consultation.
The simplest question and the most often missed: reception is busy or the clinic is closed. The agent sees the free slots and books.

clinici.faqTitle: What clinics ask before they start

faq.q: The agent will not give medical advice, will it?
faq.a: No. It does not diagnose, does not recommend treatments and does not interpret symptoms or X-rays. It answers questions about organisation and price, from the texts you write, and sends everything medical to the consultation. That is a limit written into the configuration, not a recommendation.

faq.q: What happens to patient data?
faq.a: It asks strictly what a booking needs: name, contact, reason for the visit. We do not build a medical file and we do not mix data between clinics. What the agent processes is set out in the contract and in a data processing agreement, in which the clinic is the controller.

faq.q: Our reception already has a booking program.
faq.a: The agent works inside it, if there is somewhere to connect. The point is not another calendar, it is that the free slot in your calendar also gets filled at 22:00, when reception is at home.

faq.q: How do we show cases without breaching confidentiality?
faq.a: Only with the patient's written consent and only what you have approved. The content agent publishes nothing by itself: it proposes, and you press — or you do not.

privacyPage.lead: Written for what this site actually does, not copied from somewhere. If you find something in it that does not match what you see, write to us — the mistake is ours.

sections.title: Who is responsible for the data
sections.intro: Data sent through this site is received by the controller below. Requests about your rights go to the same place.

sections.title: What data we receive
sections.intro: The site has a single form. From it we receive only what you write:
list: Your name — so we know how to address you.
Your email or phone — so we can answer.
Your company's website, if you fill it in. It is optional.
Your message, if you write one. It is optional.
sections.outro: In addition, like any site, the server logs requests: IP address, time, the page requested and the browser type. These logs are technical and are not linked to the form.

sections.title: Why we receive it
sections.intro: We use the form data to answer you and to prepare the demo or the quote you asked for — that is, for the steps before a possible contract, at your own request. Server logs exist so the site can run and be defended against abuse; the basis is our legitimate interest in keeping a service working.
sections.outro: We do not use it for anything else. If you write to us about furniture, we will not write to you a month later about something unrelated.

sections.title: Who else sees it
sections.intro: Besides us, the data passes through two services, each with a strict role:
list: Vercel — hosts the site. Requests to pages go through it, and it keeps the technical logs.
Resend — delivers the email with your request to us. The contents of the form pass through this service on the way to our mailbox.
sections.outro: We give it to nobody else. We do not sell it, trade it, or send it to advertising networks.

sections.title: Where it goes and how long we keep it
sections.intro: A form submission is not saved into a database: it leaves by email and stays in our correspondence. A database for a single form would mean backups, migrations and personal data somebody has to answer for — with no gain for you.
sections.outro: We keep the correspondence for as long as the discussion is live and for twelve months after the last message, so we can pick the conversation back up if you return. After that we delete it. Technical logs are kept by the hosting provider, for a short period, under its own rules.

sections.title: Cookies
sections.intro: The site sets a single cookie, called NEXT_LOCALE. It remembers which language you are reading in, so the next page does not send you to the wrong version. It identifies nobody and tracks nothing.
list: We have no analytics: no Google Analytics, nothing of that kind.
We have no advertising pixels and no social buttons that load somebody else's code.
Fonts are served from our own domain, not from a third-party CDN — your browser asks nothing of another server.
sections.outro: That is why the site does not greet you with a consent banner: there is nothing to consent to.

To ask us to correct what is wrong.
To ask us to delete it.
To ask us to restrict its use, or to object to use based on our legitimate interest.
To receive the data in a format that can be moved elsewhere.
sections.outro: Write to the address above and we will answer within a month at the latest. If the answer does not satisfy you, you have the right to complain to the data protection supervisory authority of the country you live in.

faq.q: What counts as a conversation?
faq.a: One visitor who wrote at least once, together with everything that followed in the same session. Ten questions in a row stay one conversation. If the same person comes back three days later, that is a second one.

faq.q: How are the phone assistant's minutes counted?
faq.a: By the second, from the moment the agent answers until the call ends. At the end of the month the seconds are added up and rounded up to a whole minute once — not per call. A 40-second call does not cost a minute.

faq.q: What happens if I go over the limit?
faq.a: Nothing stops. The agent keeps working, and anything above the limit is added as a further package at your plan's rate. We tell you when you reach 80%, so the choice is yours: an extra package, or moving to Pro.

faq.q: Can I change plan?
faq.a: Any month, in either direction. Moving to Pro applies immediately and the difference is calculated for the remaining days. Moving back to Basic applies from the following month.

faq.q: Is there a long-term contract?
faq.a: No. Monthly billing runs month by month and stops whenever you want. Annual billing is a discount for a year paid up front, not an obligation to stay.

faq.q: What happens if I cancel an annual subscription?
faq.a: We refund the unused months, recalculated at the standard monthly price. For example: you paid 1,430 € for Chatbot Pro annually and cancel after 5 months. Those 5 months are recalculated at 149 €, which is 745 €. We refund you 685 €.
